extracted.intended_audience: public relations practitioners and scholars; press-release writers and media-relations professionals
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for choosing and applying frames in press releases so journalists will accept, reproduce, and amplify the issuer's preferred angle. Focuses on seven distinct framing operations and cross-cutting quality criteria for release-level framing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Framing of situations
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the release define the situation context (a market shift, a public-health emergency, a regulatory inflection)?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pickup is much higher when the situation is named upfront so the journalist knows the story-type; use a clear situational label early (headline/lead) to signal the angle/beat.

rubrics_metrics.name: Framing of attributes
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the release foreground which attributes of the subject (a product, person, organization) it wants emphasized, and which it wants suppressed?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select specific attributes to drive the journalist's headline and slant; avoid mixed attribute signals that dilute the resulting coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Framing of choices
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the release present a choice structure (this option vs. that option, action vs. inaction)?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choice frames carry decision-relevance and increase pickup at policy/business beats; structure the story to highlight alternatives and stakes for decision-making audiences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Framing of actions
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the release frame the announcement as an action by an actor (rather than as a passive event)?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Action frames produce shorter, sharper journalist transformations—use active verbs and name actors to create crisp ledes and headlines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Framing of issues
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the release situate the story within an existing issue narrative (climate, AI safety, healthcare costs)?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Issue-framed releases attach to ongoing news waves and benefit from existing frames; tie announcements to persistent stories to gain linkage and repeat pickup.

rubrics_metrics.name: Framing of responsibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the release attribute responsibility (credit/blame) explicitly to a named actor?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Responsibility frames increase pickup at accountability beats; clearly assign actions/consequences to named entities when seeking scrutiny or praise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Framing of news
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the release pre-frame the news as news—supplying angle, 'so what,' and freshness signals—so the journalist accepts the news-frame rather than building one?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide explicit novelty/freshness cues and an immediate news hook; journalists are likelier to run a story if the release supplies a ready news-frame.

rubrics_metrics.name: Frame consistency
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the release commit to one of the seven frames primarily and use the others in support, or does it scatter across all seven?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Multi-framed releases lose pickup; prioritize a single dominant frame throughout headline, lead, and quotes to increase the likelihood of journalist adoption.

rubrics_metrics.name: Frame-fit to outcome
rubrics_metrics.description: Choose a frame that aligns with desired journalistic outcome (coverage type, downstream public response).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Match frame to receiving beat: action/responsibility for accountability beats; choice/issue for policy beats; situation/attribute for feature beats; news for breaking-news desks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Frame defensibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Is the frame one the journalist can defend to their editor, or does it require editorial cover for the issuer's bias?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A frame the journalist can defend to their editor survives; frames that appear self-serving or indefensible are likely to be stripped or reframed by reporters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Frame durability
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the release supply a frame that will continue to apply across follow-on coverage, or one that decays after the first article?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer frames that persist across subsequent stories to lock in the issuer's interpretation; avoid ephemeral framings that only work for an initial hit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Counter-frame anticipation
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the release pre-empt the most likely opposing frame?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Framing is competitive; anticipate and neutralize likely counter-frames within the release to avoid ceding the public conversation to alternative interpretations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Frame-language symmetry
rubrics_metrics.description: Do headline, lead, and quotes all reinforce the same frame?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure language across components is aligned; internal contradictions or mixed frames across headline/lead/quotes break pickup and open space for journalists to reframe.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pickup-worthiness implication
rubrics_metrics.description: A release with one clear, consistent, well-chosen frame outperforms multi-framed copy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select a single clear frame that fits the target beat and outcome; consistent framing across elements increases journalist adoption and the likelihood the coverage will follow the issuer's intended angle.
